# Build Status & Decisions Log

Moved out of `AGENTS.md` on 2026-11-23, so that the instruction file every session loads stays small (AGENTS.md, "How the rules are kept"). This file is long: search it (`git grep -n "<words>" <this file>`) and read only the lines you need, never the whole file.

Each step appends its entry at the end of this file in the same step (see "AGENTS.md updates" in `prompts/TEMPLATE.md`): what was built, the decisions, what was measured and checked, and the walk-through's results. A rule the step sets or changes goes in AGENTS.md as well, in a few lines. Newest last.

**Step 05 — Clerk authentication (2026-10-17).**

- Decisions: packages approved (versions in Tech Stack) plus `expo-constants` for Expo Go detection. `com.gracehush.app` is both `ios.bundleIdentifier` and `android.package`, with `ios.usesAppleSignIn: true` (the `expo-apple-authentication` plugin adds the entitlement itself). `app.json` stays the base config and `app.config.ts` only injects the four Google values from `process.env` into `expo.extra`, under the names in `.env.example`. No `expo-dev-client`, no `eas.json`, no prebuild: Apple and Google wait for the Clerk, Google Cloud and Apple setup.
- Added: `src/hooks/useAuthActions.ts` (the five functions, `AuthResult` unchanged, `RATE_LIMITED` and `NOT_SUPPORTED` added to `AuthErrorCode`), `app.config.ts`, `.env.example`, four strings in `copy.auth.errors`. `App.tsx` is now `App` (`ClerkProvider`, SecureStore `tokenCache`, throws a clear error when `EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` is missing) around `AppShell` (the fonts and Clerk's `isLoaded` gate the splash). `RootNavigator` switches on `isSignedIn`. `src/services/auth.ts`, `goHome()`, `onSignedIn` and every `TEMP(05)` marker are gone. The Apple button renders on iOS only.
- Email is Clerk's sign-in-or-up flow: `signIn.create({ identifier, signUpIfMissing: true })`, `emailCode.sendCode()`, `emailCode.verifyCode()`. The `sign_up_if_missing_transfer` error means a new user, so `signUp.create({ transfer: true })` and `finalize()` follow. No `signIn.reset()` is needed, because the next `create()` starts a new attempt. `signUp.missingFields` and unexpected sign-in statuses are logged in `__DEV__` only, and the user sees a calm message.
- Facts taken from the installed SDK (`@clerk/expo` 4.13.0) rather than the docs pages: the Apple and Google hooks swallow a cancelled prompt and return `createdSessionId: null`, so a null id maps to `CANCELLED` (thrown cancel codes are mapped too). The Apple hook forwards `fullName` to `signUp.create` itself, so no extra Apple call is needed for the name. The Google hook reads its IDs from `Constants.expoConfig.extra` or `process.env` and needs only the web client ID (plus the iOS one on iOS), but our guard also requires the Android client ID on Android, as the step prompt says. Network failures surface as `network_error` or `clerk_offline` (from the installed clerk-js) or as React Native's `TypeError("Network request failed")`; all three map to `NETWORK`.
- Session tasks: `finalize()` and `setActive()` get a `navigate` callback that only records `session.currentTask`. A pending task returns `extraVerification` and the user stays on Sign In. No task UI, no `taskUrls`.
- Verified: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `expo export` for Android and iOS, `expo install --check` (up to date), `expo-doctor` (21/21), and the merged config (`extra`, identifiers, plugins).
- Not verified: everything that runs. `.env.local` did not exist, so the app was never launched with Clerk: cold start and splash, email for a new and a returning user, a wrong code, resend, rate limit and airplane mode (the real network code is unconfirmed), Apple and Google in Expo Go, relaunch while signed in, sign-out, double taps, whether `isLoaded` flickers during sign-in (if it does, latch it so the navigator is not unmounted), the sheet closing on the iPhone, and the real Apple and Google flows.
- Open items: the Clerk instance settings are in the manual checklist and none could be checked from here. An instance that requires more than the email address would end a new user's sign-up at `missing_requirements`.

**Step 05 follow-up — Google in Expo Go (2026-10-17).**

- Why: the user tests on an iPhone in Expo Go, where the native Google module does not exist, so "Continue with Google" showed the "isn't available" message. They asked for it to work and approved `expo-auth-session` (57.0.16).
- What: in `useAuthActions`, `continueWithGoogle` branches on `inExpoGo` and calls Clerk's `useSSO().startSSOFlow({ strategy: "oauth_google" })`, then the same `activateSession` as the native flows. The redirect URL is Clerk's default (`AuthSession.makeRedirectUri`, `exp://…/--/sso-callback`). The native flow and its guards are unchanged for development builds. Apple is unchanged (`NOT_SUPPORTED` in Expo Go). The dev instance's own Google credentials mean no Google Cloud setup is needed for this path; a production instance would need custom credentials anyway.
- Verified on the Android emulator (Expo Go 57): Sign In shows Google and email (no Apple), tapping Google opens a Chrome custom tab on Google's "Sign in to continue to Clerk" page, so Clerk accepted the redirect URL. Closing the tab leaves the Sign In screen with no error text, and tapping Google again works. `npm run lint`, `typecheck` and `expo export` for both platforms pass.
- Not verified: completing a Google login (no credentials are entered here), the return redirect into the app and the switch to Home, and anything on the iPhone (`ASWebAuthenticationSession`). On the emulator, closing the Chrome tab returned to Expo Go's launcher list instead of the app (the app kept running and was still on Sign In); this looks like Chrome's first-run task on a fresh emulator, not an app defect, and was not checked on a device.
- Open items: if the iPhone login finishes but the app does not come back, add the redirect URL it used to "Allowlist for mobile SSO redirect" on Clerk's Native applications page.

**Step 07 — Onboarding state and permissions (2026-10-18).**

- Decisions (from the step prompt): the audio package is `expo-audio` (`getRecordingPermissionsAsync` and `requestRecordingPermissionsAsync`, never its own notification helper); a permission that can still be asked counts as `undetermined` (Android 13+ reports a never-asked notification permission as `denied` with `canAskAgain: true`); `safeStorage` and a field-by-field `merge` keep an unreadable or corrupt store from holding the splash; sign-out keeps onboarding (it is per device); both `expo-audio` background flags are `false`; the `expo-notifications` plugin gets `color` only (no `icon` until step 28 has the 96×96 white PNG, and no `enableRemoteNotifications`, which SDK 57 does not have).
- Installed with `npx expo install`: `zustand` 5.0.15, `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` 2.2.0, `expo-audio` 57.0.5, `expo-notifications` 57.0.23. Then `expo-asset` 57.0.20, approved by the user mid-step: `expo-doctor` failed 20 of 21 checks because `expo-audio` lists it as a required peer that must be a direct dependency (it was already in `node_modules` through `expo`). `expo install --check` is up to date and `expo-doctor` is 21/21. `npx expo install` exits 1 for `expo-audio` and `expo-asset` only because it cannot write a plugin into the dynamic `app.config.ts`; the plugins are added to `app.json` by hand, and no `expo-asset` plugin entry was added (the prompt allows just the two).
- **Expo Go on Android cannot import `expo-notifications`.** Found by launching the app after the first wiring: a red screen `Cannot find native module 'ExpoTopicSubscriptionModule'` (plus the expected remote-push warning from `DevicePushTokenAutoRegistration`). The Kotlin class is inside the Expo Go 57.0.9 APK but is not registered, `TopicSubscriptionModule.android.js` requires it at import time, and the package index re-exports it. 57.0.9 is the newest Expo Go for both platforms. On iOS that module is a JS stub, so the iPhone is not affected (not verified). Asked as the step required, the user chose to guard the module instead of moving Android testing to a development build: `services/notifications.ts` skips the import in Expo Go on Android only (`Platform.OS === "android" && isRunningInExpoGo()`), and its functions then answer `"undetermined"` without a prompt. iOS and development builds import it unguarded, so a real failure there is not hidden.
- Added: `src/store/onboardingStore.ts`, `src/store/safeStorage.ts`, `src/hooks/useStoreHydrated.ts`, `src/services/permissions.ts`, `recorder.ts` and `notifications.ts`, `DEFAULT_REMINDERS` and `AFFIRMATION_CHANNEL_ID` in `src/constants/app.ts`, `PermissionResult` in `src/types/index.ts`, and `copy.notifications.channelName` (the channel name is user-visible, so it lives in `copy.ts` and not inline as the prompt's snippet had it). Changed: `App.tsx` (the splash also waits for `useStoreHydrated(useOnboardingStore)`), `RootNavigator` (the three branches, the returning-user effect, `navigationKey` on SignIn), `OnboardingScreen` (reminders come from the store, `defaultTimes` and the local state are gone; "Allow & Continue" requests only `undetermined` permissions, with a ref guard and `loading` and `disabled` while it runs; "Maybe later" only completes onboarding), `HomePlaceholderScreen` (the dev reset button and helper text), `src/data/mappers.ts` (imports `DEFAULT_REMINDERS`, its private copy is deleted) and the `app.json` plugins. Both `TODO(07)` markers are gone, and nothing in `OnboardingScreen`'s markup changed.
- Differences from the prompt: (1) the Expo Go guard above. (2) `SignIn` carries a `navigationKey`. The prompt expected the navigator to return to Welcome by itself after the dev reset, and it did not: sign-out leaves the stack at `[SignIn]`, and `getStateForRouteNamesChange` keeps existing routes, so the reset only added `Onboarding` to the branch while Sign In stayed focused (a relaunch showed Welcome, so the reset itself had worked). Changing SignIn's key with the flag drops its route and the navigator falls back to `Onboarding`. (3) `useStoreHydrated` passes zustand's `onFinishHydration` and `hasHydrated` to `useSyncExternalStore` unbound, with no wrappers: the installed persist functions are closures that never use `this`. (4) `safeStorage.getItem` logs a JSON syntax error as "invalid JSON" only, because an engine's error text can quote the text it choked on.
- Native config (`app.json` plugins `expo-audio` with the microphone text, `recordAudioAndroid: true` and both background flags `false`, and `expo-notifications` with `color: "#5B3A5E"`). `npx expo config --type introspect --json` shows: `android.permissions` has `RECORD_AUDIO` and `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS` and not `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK`; `ios.infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` equals the step's string (the only place it is set); `ios.infoPlist.UIBackgroundModes` has no `audio`; `ios.entitlements["aps-environment"]` is `development` (the plugin always adds it). Config plugins only change a native build, so Expo Go ignores all of this.
- Verified: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `expo export` for Android and iOS, all exit 0, again after the last code change. A scratch harness outside the repo compiled the store, `safeStorage` and the hook and passed 75 checks: bare zustand never hydrates when a read throws, but with `safeStorage` a throwing read and invalid JSON both hydrate with the defaults and remove the bad key without logging its content; bad fields fall back while valid ones are kept; odd JSON shapes and other saved versions hydrate; `setReminder` rejects `"24:00"`, `"8:00"`, `"ab"` and more, and the same value is a no-op that keeps `remindersSyncedAt`; `completeOnboarding` and `markPermissionsPrompted` keep their first timestamp; `resetOnboarding` plus `clearStorage` removes only its own key; only the five data fields are saved; `useStoreHydrated` notifies once and stops after unsubscribing; failed writes never throw.
- Verified on the Android emulator (Expo Go 57.0.9, the prompt's checks 1 to 9, with the notification prompt out of reach there): a fresh start shows Welcome with no Sign In or Home at any sampled moment; Morning 9:30 AM survives back and forward and a force-stop, and the flow restarts at Welcome; "Allow & Continue" shows the spinner and the OS microphone prompt, and denying it lands on Sign In with no error text; a relaunch while signed out opens Sign In directly with no chevron; "I already have an account" plus email sign-in, a relaunch straight to Home, and sign-out opens Sign In without onboarding; "Maybe later" asks for nothing (neither permission carries a user-decision flag in `dumpsys`) and lands on Sign In; "Reset onboarding (dev)" shows Welcome at once, restores the defaults (Evening 8:00 PM after a saved 9:15 PM) and a relaunch still shows Welcome, so the session is gone; with both permissions granted, Expo Go showed its own per-project confirmation once, and on a second run "Allow & Continue" went straight to Sign In with no dialog. The three onboarding steps and Sign In are pixel-identical to the "before" screenshots below the status bar (re-taken on the final code).
- Not verified: the iPhone (the user confirms checks 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 in Expo Go), Gracehush's own microphone text and the notification channel on a real build (Android in step 05b, iPhone in step 35), the Android notification prompt (Expo Go cannot show it), and iOS provisional notification status.
- Open items: the manual notification icon (a white 96×96 PNG, step 28 asks for it). Step 28 and later notification steps cannot be exercised in Expo Go on Android, so they need the iPhone in Expo Go or the Android development build.

- **Deviation from the prompt, found on the emulator:** the dock's `bottom: "100%"` resolves against the parent's content box, not its border box (see the vendor note on percentage offsets), so as a child of the padded, bordered bar it overlapped the bar by the bottom inset plus the border (the mic's bottom edge was 5dp below the bar's top instead of 20dp above it). The prompt allowed `onLayout` as the fallback; a simpler fix needs no state and no height constant: `GracehushTabBar` renders an outer view with no padding or border, with the dock as its last child beside the visible bar (the inner view that carries the border, the linen background and `paddingBottom: insets.bottom`). The dock now ends 19.8dp above the bar.

The tab items stretch to the row's full 64dp height and are 56dp wide as specified; with `justify-around` the gaps between the items are not touch targets. The dock keeps its 20dp right margin under 360dp wide, where the content margin becomes 16. The fade drives both layers from one animated value (inactive 1 to 0, active 0 to 1), so at the midpoint the glyph is a little lighter than either color (about 143,123,142, against mauve 138,127,136); at 150ms this is not visible.
- Differences between the three designs, and what was built. - **Behavior beyond the prompt's text:** `useJournalHome` loads through one `useFocusEffect` whose callback depends on the scenario, and the same callback holds the `AppState` listener. So a tab that is not in front never loads, a scenario changed on Profile loads when Journal is next opened (data loaded for another scenario counts as not loaded, so the skeleton shows), the one-shot `nextHomeLoadFails` flag is spent by the load you can see, and leaving the screen drops a response that is still on its way. A load that fails with data of the same scenario on screen keeps the data and spends the flag silently (verified).

The Toast pill is `accessible` with the message as its label, inside an anchor with `pointerEvents="none"`. The heart is optimistic local state and resets when the data reloads through the loading state (persistence is `TODO(25)`). A transcript is trimmed, wrapped in curly quotes and clamped to two lines; a crisis card never reads it.

**Step 17 — Supabase and Clerk (2026-10-22).**

- Decisions (from the step prompt, approved in its review, none asked again): (1) Supabase Third-Party Auth with Clerk: the app sends Clerk's normal session token (`getToken()` with no template), so no JWT template exists and no secret is shared. (2) One package, `@supabase/supabase-js`. (3) The base schema is applied by hand, once, by the user (`supabase/schema.sql`, then `supabase/selftest.sql`); this step ran no SQL, used no management token and ran no `npx clerk config patch`. (4) The app can never write the plan: the grants are per column and the typed `Database` has no `subscription_tier` or `created_at` in its insert and update types. (5) The profile is local-first: only `profileSync` talks to the server (at sign-in, on foreground and 800 ms after a reminder edit) and `getProfile()` reads what the device already knows. (6) A development build with no Supabase values runs on the mock profile; a wrong value always stops the app and a missing one stops a release build. (7) The client and the error mapper are `src/services/supabaseClient.ts` and `src/utils/supabaseErrors.ts` (AGENTS.md has no `src/lib/`). (8) `getSupabase()` is `null` while nobody is signed in and the token callback throws `NoSessionError`, so no anonymous request can leave the app. (9) `db: { retry: false }`, so an offline read fails at once. (10) An unsent reminder edit belongs to one account: sign-out drops it, the sync never runs for a user who changed while a request was away, and the settings kept on the device are keyed by Clerk user id. **Step 21 — Crisis screening (2026-10-23).**

- Decisions (the user's "Implement it" came with a prompt that had not been through the review pass, so the reconciliation with the code and with the live API was done here, and the differences are listed below): (1) The server decides whether an entry is a crisis before it makes anything. The order is: claim, read the recording, **screen**, then (step 22) the free-tier limit, then the reflection from the screened words alone, then the passage, the save and the affirmations. The flow is in `handler.ts` (the prompt says `index.ts`, which only serves). (2) Three layers, each able to decide alone: a phrase backstop, a screening call, and the reflection's own `is_crisis` flag plus a safety block on the reflection request. `uncertain` and a block are crises, a crisis outranks a contradicting `no_speech`, and a screening that cannot be had means no reflection (the entry is failed with `AI_UNAVAILABLE` and can be sent again). (3) A recording goes to the screening once, which transcribes it and judges the words in one reply; the reflection only ever sees text, so its prompt and schema lost the audio, transcript and `no_speech` parts (`PROMPT_VERSION` is `gen-v1.2`; the screening is `screen-v1`). (4) `CONTENT_BLOCKED` no longer exists: a block is a crisis, never an error shown to the person (removed from `_shared/errors.ts`, both contract copies, `response.ts` and `mappers.ts`; no migration, because `error_code` has no check constraint). (5) The five adjustable safety filters are all `off` for the screening only (the real API accepted exactly those five). (6) The screening model is `GEMINI_SCREENING_MODEL`, else `GEMINI_MODEL` (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`); the user may set a separate one later. (7) The request log gains `screen`, `screenMs`, `screenAttempts` and `crisisSource` (one word each). (8) Nothing was deployed, no secret changed, no migration, no UI change, no package.
- Added: `supabase/functions/_shared/safety/` with `phrases.ts` (18 templates that expand to 105 phrases, a normalizer, 44 exempt idioms), `screenPrompt.ts` (`screen-v1`), `screen.ts` (`screenEntry`, `askModel`, `interpret`, `parseScreening`, the schema, the five settings), `eval/cases.json` (30 made-up entries), `eval/run_eval.ts` (by hand, real key) and the tests `phrases_test.ts`, `screen_test.ts` and `eval/cases_test.ts`.

**Step 22 — Spoken devotional and the free tier's limit (2026-10-23).**

- Decisions (the review's twelve, approved with the prompt and not changed by the build; (13) to (15) are the build's): (1) Cloud Text-to-Speech answers 401 to an API key, so the function signs in as a service account (`GOOGLE_TTS_CREDENTIALS_B64`; the token endpoint is a constant in the code and is never read from the key file). (2) Speech is optional, with three states (`readTtsConfig`: `ready`, `off` and `bad`, which names the secret), so the code, the limit and the deploy never wait for the billing: only the sound does, and it switches on with `secrets set` and no new deploy. (3) Only Chirp 3 HD voices, `markup` input and MP3 out; the language code comes from the voice name; the rate is `TTS_SPEAKING_RATE` or 0.92. (4) The script is `buildSpeechScript` of the saved row (the passage only when verified). (5) The answer carries a path and a duration and no link, and nothing stores a URL. (6) Speech runs after `ready` and is best effort: a failed call or upload sets `error_code` `TTS_FAILED`, a later success clears it, and the same request sent again runs speech only. (7) The limit is checked after the screening and before the reflection; over it the entry is saved failed with `LIMIT_REACHED`, a recording keeps the words that were heard in it, and the answer is a 402 with `entryId` and `usage`. (8) The week is Monday 00:00 on the profile's clock. (9) The speech budget is `speechTiming` and the log has 30 fields. (10) The developer check prints the plan and has the audio, retry and limit cases. (11) The known limit (the count is by creation time) is accepted. (12) No migration, package, switch in production code or `any`. **Build:** (13) The speech step is its own file, `process-entry/speech.ts`: it takes a job and gives an outcome back (it knows nothing of the request's context), never throws, and is tested on its own. (14) Once an entry is saved nothing marks it failed: `saved` is set right after `saveReadyEntry` and `saveCrisisEntry` and the `catch` skips `failEntry` then, so a database that fails while the answer is built leaves a good reflection (or a saved crisis) as it was. (15) The upload may end at most 5 s after the speech deadline.

AGENTS.md and its copy. No package, migration, secret, policy or screen changed. The fake world now answers Google's token endpoint and Text-to-Speech (a real RSA key and a real MP3 of 5,064 ms), takes a Storage upload as the real bucket does (binary, the type list, the 25 MiB limit, a duplicate without `x-upsert` refused), knows `neq`, `gt`, `lte`, `is` and `not.` filters, and keeps a strictly increasing database clock: the order of two entries made together is their creation time, and the real database never hands out one time twice.
- Differences from the prompt text, each with its reason: (1) **The time budget.** The prompt says the answer is sent before 150 s, but speech may end at 135 s and its upload was capped at 20 s after that, which is 155 s. The upload is now capped at the smaller of 20 s and 5 s past the speech deadline (`uploadCapMs`, tested, and mutation 22 is caught), so the worst case is about 145 s. (2) **Case p** is tested on `checkDevotionalLimit` itself with a pinned clock (`checkLimit_test.ts`: 15 scenarios, the tiers, the third-or-fourth rule, two zones, a bad zone and a failing query), not through the handler; the handler tests j, m, o, q and r cover the same rules end to end, and `weekly_test.ts` stays about the arithmetic of the week. (3) **Case u, the crisis arm.** After `saveCrisisEntry` the handler makes no database call (a crisis answer is built from the row and has no affirmations to read), so no database failure can reach the flag there: `saved u2` proves the handler needs no database after a crisis is saved, and `saved u` (a failing affirmations read after a reflection and its audio were saved) proves the flag. The flag is set after the crisis save as well, for code added later. (8) The check's closing line counts skips (`Done: 14 passed, 3 skipped.`) and reads as before when none is skipped. (9) Test names carry words (`speech b)`, `limit j) m)`, `log s)`, `saved u)`) because the file already uses the letters a to m for other cases.

**Step 22 follow-up 3 — the fonts after the SDK 58 upgrade (2026-10-24).**

- What happened: on the iPhone (Expo Go 58) every text drew in the iOS system font. Colours, sizes and spacing were right, so NativeWind's classes compiled, and the compiled styles named `Fraunces_600SemiBold` and the others (checked in the iOS bundle). The user's screenshots from before the upgrade, Fraunces on every heading and card, were the target.
- How it was found: nothing on this machine was wrong (the dev server serves all eight TTFs through the exact URL expo-asset 58 builds, with the same bytes and hash, on all three URL implementations the app can be running; expo-font 58's iOS alias code resolves a single-face alias as 57 did; the eight font files are static), so the running app on the phone was read through the dev server's Hermes inspector (`/json/list`, then `Runtime.evaluate` over a WebSocket, read-only): `ExpoFontLoader.getLoadedFonts()` was `[]`, `Asset.fromModule` threw `Cannot read property 'getAssetByID' of undefined`, react-native's exports held `AssetRegistry` while NativeWind's wrapper (the module expo-asset's `react-native` import resolved to) did not, and loading the eight fonts through the real registry registered all eight, so download, cache and CoreText registration are fine. The cause is the NativeWind vendor note above.
- Changed: `metro.config.js` (the resolver bypass for `node_modules/expo-asset/`) and `App.tsx` (a development-only `console.warn` when `useFonts` reports an error; the gate's behaviour is unchanged). The temporary font readout added to `DevToolsPanel.tsx` during the diagnosis was removed (the file is byte-identical to before). No dependency, token or screen changed.
- Verified: in the dev bundle expo-asset's `Asset.js` now depends on `react-native/index.js` while `PrimaryButton.tsx` and `JournalFeedScreen.tsx` keep the react-native-css wrapper, and the compiled font families are unchanged; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` exit 0; `expo export` for iOS (71 s) and Android (73 s) exit 0, and in the iOS export expo-asset's module depends on the react-native index module. A first version of the bypass matched the origin path with a regex written through a shell heredoc that lost a backslash, so it never matched a Windows path (found with a trace in the resolver and a bundle of expo-asset alone); the file now compares with `path.join(__dirname, "node_modules", "expo-asset") + path.sep`.
- Not verified: the permanent fix on the iPhone. The user's next screenshot (the Journal with the Filter sheet open, 4:56 PM) shows Fraunces and DM Sans, but it does not prove the fix: the dev server on port 8081 (started 15:30) predates the new `metro.config.js` (16:40), and Expo's CLI only watches that file to print a warning, it does not restart Metro (`FileNotifier` in `@expo/cli` 58.1.15); and the diagnosis had registered the eight fonts under the app's own aliases inside the running Expo Go process through the inspector. Those registrations are process-wide native state (CoreText's process scope, and a file-level alias table in expo-font's Swift code, read in `FontFamilyAliasManager.swift`, not tested), so they probably survive a JS reload and would hide a failing `useFonts` until Expo Go is force-quit. The test that proves the fix: restart the dev server with `npx expo start -c`, force-quit Expo Go on the iPhone, reopen the project, and look for Fraunces headings on the Journal with no `[fonts] …` warning in the terminal. Everything before that is proven: the registry reaches expo-asset in the new bundle, and the fonts register on the phone once it does.

**Step 23 — Voice recording (2026-10-24).**

- Decisions (the review's 15, approved with the prompt by the user's "Implement it"; none struck): (1) `expo-file-system` and `expo-keep-awake` are the only two packages. (2) No native change: `app.json` is untouched, with no prebuild, no `eas.json` and no development build; foreground recording runs in Expo Go. (3) One imperative recorder service (`services/recorder.ts`), not `useAudioRecorder`: the native recorder is made when a take starts and released when it ends, with its options from `createRecordingOptions` (a deep import of `expo-audio/build/utils/options`: if a later SDK moves that file, build the options inline). (4) Interruptions pause and only a tap resumes: the app takes the library's own pause over (see the `expo-audio` 58 vendor note). (5) The screen stays awake while a take runs (tag `gracehush-recording`). (6) The finished file is moved to `recordings/{clientEntryId}.m4a` the moment the take ends, and a take under 1 KB is a failed recording. (7) A fixed in-progress name (`recording-in-progress`), so a take that was never stopped leaves one fragment, overwritten by the next take; sign-out cannot clean that fragment (a known, bounded limit). (8) `useRecorder(clientEntryId)` also returns `resume` and a `paused` state, with nothing removed or renamed; New Entry makes its one id before the hook. (9) The phone refuses to upload a file over 12 MiB, the function's own limit, measured on the file. (10) The upload is `{ ok: true, path }` or `{ ok: false, code }` with no message (`NETWORK`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `TOO_LARGE`, `NOT_FOUND`, `UNKNOWN`), with one retry after 1.5 s for `NETWORK` only, and an object that is already there counts as success. (11) Sign-out and account deletion delete every finished recording (`signOutCleanup()` calls `deleteAllRecordings()`). (12) Haptics: a resume ticks like a start (`light`), a finish from paused like a stop (`medium`), and the automatic pause makes none. (13) Other apps' audio keeps playing while a take runs (the default interruption mode); step 26 owns the audio session from here. (14) Four new strings in `copy.newEntry.speak` (`captionPaused`, `resumeLabel`, `paused`, `errors.resume`) and a "Recordings (dev)" group in the developer panel. (15) Flagged, not decided: the finished takes live in the document folder, which iOS includes in iCloud and computer backups, and keeping them out needs a file attribute that `expo-file-system` 58 does not expose: revisit it with the queue in step 24.

**Step 24 — Offline cache and sync (2026-10-25).**

- Decisions (the review's 12, approved with the prompt by the user's "Implement it"; none struck): (1) Two packages, `expo-sqlite` and `@react-native-community/netinfo` (`await-lock` came with `expo-sqlite`), and no native change: no prebuild, no `eas.json`, no development build, nothing in `app.json`. (2) The words are encrypted by the app: AES-256-GCM through expo-crypto's native AES, one random key per user in SecureStore (`gracehush.dbkey.{hash}`, `WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`). SQLCipher is not used (expo-sqlite's docs say it is unavailable in Expo Go). The words are encrypted, the bookkeeping is not. (3) One database file per user, `gracehush-{first 16 hex of SHA-256(userId)}.db`, one connection, migrations by `PRAGMA user_version` in one transaction (a file from a newer app is refused and left alone), and opens, closes and deletes run one at a time; the raw user id is never in a file name, a key name or a log. (4) Schema version 1: `outbox`, `entries_cache` and `affirmations_cache`. There is no `audio_uri` column (a voice entry's file is rebuilt from its id) and no `meta` table; `server_entry_id` and `limit_resets_at` keep what the 402 says; every query binds its values. (5) The sync engine: one run at a time, oldest first, only while the app is in front, the phone can send and the database is open; a generation counter, so nothing lands after sign-out; a call that never answers counts as `NETWORK` after 200 s; one failure table (`retry`, `limit`, `pause_auth`, `needs_action`; an unknown code is retried, never dropped) with backoff 5 s, 15 s, 60 s, 5 min, 15 min, then 1 h, 20% jitter, and at least 60 s after `RATE_LIMITED` and 30 s after `ALREADY_PROCESSING`. (6) One processor interface, `services/entryProcessor.ts` (`processItem`, `processorIsMock`), over the mock `processMock` (`TEMP(25)`), which answers the dev store's `nextSubmitOutcome` (now with `too_short`) or, once, no answer (`nextNetworkFails`); while the processor is a mock nothing is written to the read cache. (7) Journal lists unsent reflections as entry-shaped cards above the entries (`HomeEntry`), never with their words, with the status lines, **Review** and **See plans**; two calm banner kinds, never toasts; the synced toast only when nothing is left to send. (8) New Entry saves first, then waits for the engine up to 90 s with the existing overlay; its failure view has two kinds (the phone could not save it, or the server refused it); "Saved locally" is removed from its header (a visual change to an approved screen, flagged in the prompt and not struck). (9) Sign-out and account deletion delete the user's database and its key; deletion does not ask about unsent items. (10) A recording with no outbox item that is over 7 days old is deleted once per launch. (11) A reflection the free limit holds goes again when the plan is paid (`getKnownTier()`, and `resumeAfterUpgrade()` after a purchase or a restore) or when its week ends. (12) Flagged, not decided: (a) the database and the recordings live in the document folder, which iOS includes in iCloud and computer backups; the words are sealed with a key that is not in backups, so a restored phone resets the file, but the bookkeeping and the recordings are in the backup; (b) if a session ends without a sign-out and a different account signs in on the phone, the first account's queued recordings have no item in the second account's database and are cleaned after 7 days (per-account recording folders would fix it, later).

**Step 26 follow-up — an offline play no longer waits (2026-10-27).**

- What happened: in the walk-through's B10(b) a devotional that was not on the phone, played in Airplane mode, kept its spinner for 4 minutes 13 seconds with no "Audio needs a connection." line, and when the connection came back the download finished and the devotional started by itself (the player log: the press at 17:01:06, the sound at 17:05:19, 2026-10-26). Nothing limited how long the download link could take, and with no connection the request waited, either for a Clerk session token that could not be refreshed (step 18 saw a token request hang offline for minutes) or for Storage itself. Which one was not established, and the fix covers both.
- Decision (the user's yes to the recommendation, 2026-10-27): (1) A devotional that is not on the phone while NetInfo says there is no connection (`selectCanSend` false: not connected, or no internet) answers `NETWORK` at once without asking for a link, so the store shows "offline". A saved devotional still plays offline. A failed request elsewhere (`unreachable`) does not count, so a stale flag cannot block a play that would work. (2) The link gets 15 seconds (`DEVOTIONAL_LINK_TIMEOUT_MS`); after that it counts as `NETWORK` and its late answer is dropped, so it can never start a download or a devotional. The download itself gets no new limit: a slow first play over a weak connection is not cut off.
- Changed: `src/services/devotionalAudio.ts` (`signedLink` races the request against the limit; `fetchFile` reads the offline store after the saved-file check), `src/constants/audio.ts` (`DEVOTIONAL_LINK_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) and `supabase/tests/playback/run.cjs` (four checks: two on the file, and two run on both the iOS and the Android fake player, 133 in all). The store, the copy and the screens are unchanged. Nothing was installed.
- Verified: playback 133. Each of the two parts, removed in a scratch copy (a control run first, 133), fails exactly its own three checks: without the offline check "file: while the phone is known to be offline a saved devotional still plays, and one not saved answers NETWORK at once with no link asked" and "known to be offline, play says "offline" at once and nothing starts when the connection returns" on both platforms; without the limit "file: a link that has not come after 15 seconds answers NETWORK, and its late answer is never used" and "a link that never comes stops the spinner after 15 seconds, and its late answer starts nothing" on both. Recording 68, offline 44 of 44, profile-sync 88, journal-data 86, parity 7 of 7, and typecheck and lint exit 0. On the iPhone (B10(b) again, the 9:46 AM devotional, never played): "Audio needs a connection." 24 ms after the press and after two more presses, and nothing played or downloaded when Airplane mode went off.

**Step 26 follow-up 2 — the scrubber's drag and the status bar in modals (2026-10-27).**

- What happened: (1) On the iPhone the Now Playing scrubber stopped following the finger part-way through a drag (B2). The user's test confirmed the cause: dragging sideways with the finger sliding a little downward, the whole sheet moved down with the finger when the thumb stopped. iOS's page sheet hands a touch that drifts downward to its swipe-to-close gesture, which cancels the JavaScript drag; the page's `scrollEnabled={false}` cannot stop it, and Android has no such gesture (the emulator never showed it). (2) Once Now Playing was full screen, its Close row sat under the status bar (the clock covered it), and the user had seen the same on New Entry's X on and off across reloads. The cause is in react-native-safe-area-context's iOS code (the vendor note on safe areas in modals): a `SafeAreaView` in a modal reads its inset once, sometimes before the modal is in place, and never again.
- Decisions (the user's yes after the test, and "fix that UI bug across the app on all screens applicable"): (1) Now Playing is `fullScreenModal` on iOS and stays `modal` on Android, still sliding up from the bottom; the iOS grab handle is gone and Close closes it. The cost is the swipe-down to close on the iPhone, judged smaller than a close gesture that takes the scrubber's drag. Rebuilding the scrubber on `react-native-gesture-handler` (installed, unused) was considered and not chosen: it needs approval, root views in the app and in the modal, and it could not be shown to win the touch from the sheet. (2) Every modal screen gets its own `SafeAreaProvider` through the navigator's `layout` (New Entry, Now Playing, Support Resources and the Paywall), and so do the two `Modal`s that hold a `SafeAreaView` (`BottomSheet` and `ReminderTimePicker`, bottom edge). `ConfirmDialog` has none. The tabs, Reflection, Sign In and Onboarding sit under the root provider and were never affected.
- Changed: `src/navigation/RootNavigator.tsx` (`nowPlayingOptions`, `modalLayout` and `layout={modalLayout}` on the four modal screens), `src/screens/journal/NowPlayingScreen.tsx` (the iOS grab handle removed), `src/components/BottomSheet.tsx` and `src/components/ReminderTimePicker.tsx` (a provider inside the `Modal`). Nothing installed; no copy, store or test changed; each file kept its line endings.
- Verified: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` exit 0, and the 133 playback checks pass. On the iPhone in Expo Go, after a force-quit and again after a Reload, the user reported all fixed: Now Playing opens full screen with Close below the clock, a sideways drag that slides downward keeps the thumb under the finger to the end, the screen does not swipe away, and Close returns to the reflection still playing; New Entry's X (from the mic and from the pen) sits below the clock; the Journal's Filter sheet keeps its button above the home bar.

**Step 28 follow-up — the plan waits for the newest reflection's affirmations (2026-10-28).**

- What happened (B11 of the walk-through above): after a sign-in, Journal's first page asked for the affirmation plan before `getLatestAffirmations()` had fetched the newest reflection's affirmations and written them to the phone. Sign-out deletes the phone's copy, so the plan, half a second later, read the newest reflection without its three headlines, scheduled nothing (decision 3), and nothing asked again when they arrived a second or two later. The same order would cancel what is scheduled when a reflection made on another phone reaches this one first, until the app next comes to the front.
- Decision (the user's yes to the recommendation, 2026-10-28): Journal asks for the plan after `getLatestAffirmations()` has answered, which writes the affirmations to the cache, and not before. Nothing else changes: a reflection that lacks a headline still gets no notifications (decision 3).

**Step 29b — Remove from Prayers, and delete a reflection (2026-10-28).**

- Decisions (the prompt's 12, approved with it by the user's "Implement your professional recommendation you just gave." and "Implement it."; none struck): (1) every Active and Answered prayer has a ⋯ menu with two different actions: **Remove from Prayers** (the step 29 `setPrayerTracked(false)` patch: it clears the flags and an answered date and note, keeps the reflection, is queued and works offline; only an Answered prayer asks first) and **Delete reflection…** (permanent, online only, always asks); Reflection gets a quiet "Delete reflection" link at the end of its ready view; (2) the delete runs in the new Edge Function `delete-entry` (service role, `verify_jwt = false`, the Clerk token checked by `_shared/auth.ts`), because the app keeps no DELETE grant and Storage keeps no delete policy; (3) it is online only and nothing is queued; (4) a server-only table `deleted_devotionals` keeps the free week honest: **it records deleted devotionals only** (written by `delete-entry` just before it deletes the row, not a ledger of every devotional made), `checkDevotionalLimit` adds this person's records made from the week's start to the reflections that exist, so deleting does not give a free devotional back; it needs no backfill and leaves `process-entry`'s creation path alone; (5) crisis red on Prayers for the Delete row and the dialog's confirm button only (it replaces step 14's "no crisis red on this screen, no red option"); (6) scope: Prayers and Reflection; Journal cards get no delete, and a crisis entry cannot be deleted from the app (crisis handling is asked about first); (7) Remove from Prayers asks only for an Answered prayer (it destroys the gratitude note); (8) no swipe, no undo, no trash folder, no haptic; (9) after the server has deleted it the phone forgets every copy in a fixed order (the cached entry with its affirmations and its waiting prayer change, the player if that devotional is loaded, its downloaded file, the lists on screen through the new `deleted` sync event, and the notifications are planned again); (10) on the server: files, then the record, then the row, each step treating "already done" as done, `NOT_FOUND` meaning already deleted; (11) no rate limit; (12) nothing installed.

React Native 0.88's `RCTModalHostViewComponentView.mm` presents a Modal at once with no queue and emits `onDismiss` when the dismissal completes, so a choice that opened its Modal in the same tick as the sheet's closing would not appear (the "fragile case" the vendor notes already record). So `BottomSheet` has an optional `onDismiss`, `PrayersScreen` keeps the choice in a ref (`afterMenu`) and goes on from `onDismiss` on iOS, with a `MODAL_HANDOFF_FALLBACK_MS` (1 second) timer in case iOS never reports it (it runs once, whichever is first); Android has no event and overlaps its dialogs fine, so it goes on at once. See the Bottom Sheets rule.

**Step 33 — Realtime (2026-10-31).**

- Decisions: the prompt's 15, approved with it by the user's "Implement it."; none struck. Added in the build, each with its reason: (16) the affirmations message is `{ id, entry_id }`, not `{ entry_id }`: the hosted `realtime.send` adds a random `id` to a payload that has none (Supabase's Realtime migration of 2026-06-05), so the trigger sends the affirmation's own id instead; the app's guard still reads only `entry_id`. (17) A failed channel shows `offline` with a one-word reason while it waits to try again (`unauthorized`, `private_only`, `timed_out`, `closed`, `channel_error`), and `connecting` only while it asks for the token or waits for the join, as the prompt's table F describes; a stop shows `offline` with the condition's word (`background`, `offline`, `no_database`, `mock_data`, `force_polling`, `signed_out`, `stopped`). (18) Reflection shows "not found" on the Realtime DELETE event, not on the sync engine's `deleted` event (the prompt's 4.5): a delete made on Reflection itself announces `deleted` and then leaves the screen (`useDeleteReflection`, then `goBack`), and following that event would show "This reflection couldn’t be found." during the back transition. A Realtime delete calls `forgetOnThisPhone` first, so both lists and the screen agree. (19) `fetchEntry` and `fetchAffirmations` take an optional `keep` check (always true by default): a read Realtime started writes nothing once Realtime has stopped, so a first account's late answer can never land in the next account's database after a sign-out. (20) Only a reflection that has just finished (not ready in the cache before) reads its affirmations, plans the notifications and wakes a queued outbox item; a change to a reflection that was already finished (a prayer change, a heart, often this phone's own) reads the entry only. A finished reflection whose message is skipped as not newer still wakes its queued item (one SQLite update, no network), because a Journal load can cache the finished row before its message arrives. (21) Journal moves the known total both ways: a listed entry joins the loaded range with one more (an older one is left for its page), and an entry that stops being listed (a failed one) leaves with one fewer; without the second, B5 to B7 would end one too high while Journal is in front. (22) Journal asks for the run of days again only when an entry turned ready (from the list it shows), not on every message. (23) `resync` follows any drop while the app stays in front (a failed channel, the phone offline, Force polling, the mock data, the database closed), not only a failed channel: the screens' own reloads (focus, a return to the front) cover none of these; going to the background clears it. (24) While the channel is live the app checks the session token every 5 s and renews one with 15 s or fewer left from Clerk's server (`REALTIME_TOKEN_CHECK_MS`, `REALTIME_TOKEN_RENEW_S`; `startTokenChecks` on `SUBSCRIBED`, stopped by every stop and failure and, as further guards, by the generation counter in the timer and in the check): the prompt and the review's vendor note relied on Realtime's own refresh at its 25 s heartbeat, which the walk-through showed to come too late (the token fix, below).

- The token fix (found in the walk-through; the user's "go ahaead with the fix", 2026-10-31): during B3 and B4 the channel dropped twice with `closed` while the app stayed in front (reconnects 2). A read-only recorder on the phone (the seconds left on the token Realtime held, from its `exp` claim, never the token itself) showed why: the token reached 1 s left and the server closed the channel when it expired. clerk-js 6.39.1 refreshes its cached token in a background fetch 17 s before expiry (`w-15-2` in its native build) and hands back the old token until 5 s are left, while Realtime asks again only at its heartbeat every 25 s. First fix: `setAuth()` every 10 s while live. On the phone (B5, about 15 minutes, 20 token cycles) it replaced the token with 5 to 16 s left 19 times, but once Clerk's background refresh did not land in time and the token expired again (reconnects 1, `closed` at 0 s left), and once it landed late (5 s left): a check every 10 s can miss the last 5 s, the only time Clerk fetches a new token by itself. Second fix, the code now: a check every 5 s (`REALTIME_TOKEN_CHECK_MS`) that, when Clerk's cached token has 15 s or fewer left (`REALTIME_TOKEN_RENEW_S`), asks Clerk's server for a new one (`renewSessionTokenIfExpiring` in `supabaseClient.ts`, `getToken({ skipCache: true })`, no template; the auth bridge passes the option through) and then pushes with `setAuth()` (`checkToken`, `startTokenChecks` and `stopTokenChecks` in `realtime.ts`). Checks: "token: while the channel is live the token is checked every 5 s, and never while it is stopped, joining or failed" (it also counts every read of Clerk's token, so a timer left running is seen), "token: a token with 15 s or fewer left is renewed by Clerk's server before it is pushed, a failed renewal is tried at the next check, and a fresh token is not renewed", and the real-library check now needs the new token on the channel within 5 s, before the first heartbeat, and only once (realtime 27 checks, offline 44 of 44, profile-sync 88, typecheck and lint 0). Breakages in a scratch copy, 12 of 12 caught by a named check: no checks at all, a 10 s period, the token passed in (Realtime then never asks Clerk again), checks started before the join succeeds, a stop and a failure that each leave the checks running (with the timer's generation guard removed too), no renewal, a renewal through Clerk's cache, a renewal only at 4 s, the push before the renewal, a failed renewal that skips the push, and a fresh token renewed too. The first run of them found two survivors: a timer left running pushed nothing, because the check's own generation guard stopped it, but it still read Clerk's token every 5 s; the cadence check now counts those reads.

(2) Two in-app marks in `src/constants/images.ts`: `logoMark`, plum and rose, for linen, white and blush surfaces (the header emblem, the Sign In tile, the Journal empty state, the Paywall hero), and `logoMarkLight`, white and rose, for the brand gradient and plum surfaces (the onboarding hero tile, the Now Playing artwork tile, the processing orb). Both are PNG, 456 × 456, the mark at its native pixels and 72% of the square (the old SVG mark spanned about 71% of its 48-box), so every `Image` box keeps the size the designs gave it (32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 56) and the tiles keep their visual weight. The five `tintColor` calls went: a tint flattens a two-tone mark to a silhouette, and the light file is what a white tint used to do. (3) The app icon set, all from the same mark: `icon.png` 1024 × 1024, opaque on `linen` with the mark 58.5% tall and 46% wide (iOS refuses alpha in an icon; the template's glyph sat at 42%); `assets/expo.icon` is a new Icon Composer document with the template's own keys (an `automatic-gradient` fill in linen, one PNG layer `Assets/logo-mark.png`, a neutral shadow at 0.5, translucency off so the plum stays plum; the Expo symbol and its grid went); `android-icon-foreground.png` and `android-icon-monochrome.png` 1024 × 1024 with the mark 45% tall (the hand tips are 307 px from the centre, inside the 313-px radius of Android's 66-dp safe circle) on `backgroundColor` linen (the template's `backgroundImage` and its 512-px file went); `splash-icon.png`, the mark at twice its native size on transparency, shown at `imageWidth` 120 (so 150 dp tall) on a linen splash, so the icon, the splash and the first screen are one continuous surface (the plum splash with the Expo logo at 76 went); `favicon.png` 64 × 64 for the web output nobody ships. The header's initials are Fraunces Medium 13/16, Profile's stay `text-headline` (24/32), and the icon is 18 and 28. Two faults. (1) A layout bug, not a wording one: the list sat `self-center` inside wrappers under `items-center`, so its width was auto; a line longer than the column was never asked to wrap, the block grew to the longest line and overflowed, centred (the second row on the final step wrapped at about 420 dp, the longest row's width, not the column's 350). **Crisis entries can be deleted (2026-11-01).**

- What happened: the user saw a crisis entry's card ("A heavy moment. Tap to see support.") on the Journal with no way to delete it, where every other reflection can be deleted from its screen, and said a person might want to delete it at any time. - Assessment: it was a missing door, not a wall. The server's `delete-entry` deletes a crisis row like any other (it reads the crisis flag only to skip the free-week record, which a crisis never had), and no client guard refused one: the entry was undeletable only because no screen offered the action. Nothing in the app depends on the entry staying: the app keeps no other record of a crisis, never contacts anyone, and already lets the person delete the whole account; an undeletable "heavy moment" card on the home screen is a privacy problem for anyone who glances at the phone.
- Decision (the user's yes to the recommendation): the crisis view ends with the same quiet "Delete reflection" link as the ready view, under "Return to Journal", so it never competes with the help above it: mauve, never red, 44 dp, the hint "Asks before deleting", online only with the same calm offline line. The shared dialog gets a body for this entry, "This permanently deletes what you shared. This can’t be undone." (`copy.deleteReflection.bodyCrisis`: a crisis entry has no devotional, audio or affirmations to name), chosen by a new `crisis` flag on `useDeleteReflection`'s target and dialog state. After the delete the screen goes back as the chevron does, the card leaves the list, and the notifications are planned again from the reflection before it: the quiet a crisis entry imposes on the affirmations ends with its deletion, because keeping it would need a local record of a crisis, which the rules forbid everywhere else. No haptic, no sound, no log line, and no analytics event: Reflection's deletion callback skips `reflection_deleted` for a crisis entry. Support Resources has no delete, and a Journal card has none of its own (the ⋯ on every card is still the open item from step 29b).

**The reset of the free week is a date (2026-11-02).**

- What happened: on Monday, November 2, the user's Journal showed two reflections from the night before while Profile read "0 of 3 audio devotionals used this week" and "Resets Monday", and they asked for the cause before any fix. Read from the phone through the dev server's inspector, read-only (the app's own `getProfile`, `weekWindow`, `readCachedEntries`, `listEntriesSince`, `countDevotionalsSince` and `getUsage`): the profile's zone and the device's both Africa/Lagos; the week Monday Nov 2 00:00 to Monday Nov 9 00:00 Lagos; the two reflections made 2026-11-01T21:15Z and 2026-11-01T20:10Z (Sunday 10:15 PM and 9:10 PM Lagos, 1.74 and 2.82 hours before the week began), both ready with a devotional and audio; the database open and the week's query answering both rows, which rules out the failed-read path (it answers 0 too); the count 0 and the usage 0 of 3. Not a counting bug: the free week runs Monday to Monday on the profile's clock, the server's own rule (step 22, decision 8), and the two reflections belong to last week. What made it look wrong was the wording: "Resets Monday" on a Monday reads as today, and nothing said the week had begun at midnight.
- Decision (the user's yes to the one recommendation): the reset is shown as a date in the three places that name it: Profile "Resets Monday, Nov 9", the Paywall's limit banner "They reset Monday, Nov 9." and a held Journal card "Saved · Unlocks with Pro or on Monday, Nov 9". `formatResetDay` in `utils/format.ts` (the long weekday, the short month and the day, in the phone's zone like every other date the app formats) replaces `formatWeekday`; the three copy builders keep their names and their parameter is `resetDay`. **Launch screen (2026-11-03).**

- What happened: in B1 of the step 35 walk-through the user put the launch screen beside YouVersion's on the iPhone, said the logo was boring and too big, and asked for it to be fixed as a top company would. Measured from the two screenshots on the 414-point-wide screen: Gracehush's mark 91.8 by 114.9 points at 50.0% of the height on linen, YouVersion's icon 71.5 by 72.2 points at 45.9% on near-black. The plugin fits an image into a square box of `imageWidth` (`withIosSplashAssets.js`: width and height both `imageWidth * ratio`), so the old tall image's `imageWidth` of 120 acted as its height.
- Decisions (the user's request; the look chosen from rendered mock-ups beside YouVersion's screenshot): (1) `plum-deep` (`#3E2741`) as the launch background, not linen: a strong brand colour, and kinder than linen at night. Primary `plum` was tried and reads lighter and less premium, with less contrast for the rose. (2) A brand lockup, the mark 64 points tall (52 wide, under YouVersion's 72) over the two-tone "GraceHush" at 24 points, 14 apart: 125 by 96 points. Colours are linen and rose, with the mark's white moved to linen so the mark and the name match. The name is the header wordmark's face and tracking (Fraunces SemiBold, -2.5%), rendered by headless Edge from the app's own font file because this Pillow has no raqm, so it has the font's kerning. (3) A square canvas (600 by 600, stored at 3x, `imageWidth` 200), so the width is exact. The lockup sits 22 points above the canvas's centre, because the storyboard centres the image and the true centre looks low on a tall phone. (4) Flat, as the large apps' launch screens are: tried and not built, a soft glow behind the flame and the app icon in a tile. No "from ..." line: it helps when the parent brand is well known, and the plugin has one centred image (reversed on 2026-11-19 at the owner's request: the launch screen now says "from Nouvrix", its own entry). (5) The launch screen now fades into the first screen over 400 ms (`SplashScreen.setOptions`, skipped in Expo Go, which warns), where it used to cut. No custom animation. (6) The clock is white over the plum (`UIStatusBarStyle` `UIStatusBarStyleLightContent`, since `UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance` is false) and turns dark, animated, at the moment the gate opens and the fade starts (`ready` in `App.tsx`). (7) The mark's shape, the Home Screen icon and the Android adaptive icon are unchanged.

**Production Supabase, secrets, deploy and an end-to-end test on the iPhone (2026-11-06).**

- Decisions (the owner's, after a cost discussion): (1) Production is a SEPARATE Supabase project, created inside the owner's existing Supabase organization, which was upgraded to Pro that day (an empty second organization that had been made for the purpose was deleted first; the Free plan allows two active projects per person, which had blocked a third, and the upgrade lifts that limit). Reasons for two projects: the Edge Functions accept ONE Clerk issuer (`CLERK_ISSUER`) and one `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, so one project cannot serve both the development and the production Clerk instance; test data must not mix with real people's prayers; the secrets differ. (2) Region us-east-1 (the same as the development project, and the Privacy Policy says production data is in the US), Micro compute, Data API on, "Automatically expose new tables" off and automatic RLS off (the migrations grant explicitly), no GitHub integration, and a dashboard-generated database password that only the owner holds (no command that needs it is used against this project, and the dashboard can reset it). (3) Cost, from Supabase's docs (read 2026-11-06): in a Pro organization every running project is billed as a Micro, about $10 a month (the Free plan's Nano included), the $10 compute credit is per ORGANIZATION, paused projects are not billed, and a project in a Pro organization CANNOT be paused. So the old development project has counted as $10 since the upgrade and the production project brings the total to about $45 a month. Moving the development project into a free organization (project settings, General, Transfer project) would keep the total at about $35 (that project would then be on the Free plan, where it can be paused and auto-pauses after a week idle); the owner declined it and keeps both in the Pro organization. The docs do not say whether a transfer keeps a project's address and keys, so probe before and after if it is ever done.
- Built: all 7 migrations as ONE script pasted into the SQL editor (every file in order, plus a read-only query that lists the tables and buckets; no migration file contains transaction control, so the paste is all-or-nothing); `selftest.sql` 11 of 11; `rls_selftest.sql` 64 checks, 61 passed, 3 skipped (checks 60 to 62 need a Realtime client to have connected that day), 0 failed. The production Clerk instance is registered under Authentication, Third-Party Auth (its Frontend API URL, which equals the token's `iss`). Realtime: the service on, "Allow public access to channels" off. Secrets (14): the 10 shared with development copied unchanged (the Gemini key and its two models, the Text-to-Speech credentials, voice and rate, the RevenueCat V1 secret key, and the three Sign in with Apple values), `CLERK_ISSUER` (production), a NEW dedicated `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` (an `sk_live_` key made for this purpose; Clerk shows a secret key only once, at creation), and for a NEW RevenueCat webhook named for production its own `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH` (generated here) and its own `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET`. The secrets live in a private folder OUTSIDE the repository: the functions secrets file, the app's public settings file for production and a Windows `.cmd` that runs `secrets set --env-file` and the seven `functions deploy ... --use-api`, naming only the production project. The owner ran it from the committed code. The new secrets reached their file through clipboard watchers: a script waits for a value of the expected shape (`sk_live_`, 64 hex characters, `sb_publishable_`), appends `NAME=value` to the file without printing it, and clears the clipboard.
- Checks without a phone: unauthenticated probes answer as the development functions do: the six that take a Clerk token give 401 with the function's own error word (a made-up bearer token too), 405 for a GET and 204 for a browser preflight, and the webhook gives 405 for a GET and 401 without its Authorization value; a signed TEST event sent to the webhook (HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<body>`, both secrets read in memory from the private file) answers 200, and a wrong signature or a wrong Authorization value answers 401; RevenueCat's own "Send test event" to the new webhook answers 200.
- End-to-end test (the owner's real production accounts; the agent read the app through the Hermes inspector and the owner only tapped): the iPhone development build ran against production through a SECOND Metro server on another port, started with the four production `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values set in the shell (the owner's own dev server was left alone). In development mode Expo does not bake `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` into Metro's transform cache (the serializer injects them for each bundle; read in `node_modules`), so two servers with different values can share the cache. The served bundle was counted: the production values appear once each, the development address never, and no real secret (the `sk_` and `sb_secret_` strings in it are the app's own guards and library checks). Results on production: native Apple sign-in; the token has the production issuer and the `authenticated` role; the profile row was created under RLS; Realtime live (6 events, no reconnect); a made-up written reflection `ready` in 29 s with 100 s of audio, a verified verse and 3 affirmations (so Gemini, the Bible API, Text-to-Speech, Storage and every secret work); playback from production storage (heard); the export (a valid ZIP of 4.8 MB, a one-hour link); native Google sign-in as a second account, which sees 0 of the first account's rows (RLS isolation); `sync-subscription` 200 (free plan); and `delete-account` 200 (which needs the live Clerk secret key). Not tested: Apple's revocation on production, a Test Store purchase through the production webhook, notification delivery, a release build, VoiceOver and Android. The Apple test account and its reflection remain in production.

It holds no RevenueCat Test Store key (a release build refuses it) and no RevenueCat iOS key yet (section H of prompt 35). `eas.json` gained a `production` profile (store distribution, the production environment, `autoIncrement`; the version source was already remote), and `eas config --profile production` resolves it and loads exactly those 8. The release gate printed nothing before the first store build. A store build asks for the Apple login again (it needs an App Store provisioning profile): the first attempt used a different Apple ID and failed with "no team associated" after a good 2FA; with the developer account's ID it reused the existing distribution certificate.

**The verse card flows (2026-11-07).**

- What happened: the owner opened a reflection in the TestFlight build (build 6) and sent a screenshot of the Scripture card for Isaiah 30:15, saying the verse was not properly formatted and was in a mess. The cause: the card passed the Bible's own poetry line breaks straight to the text. The first line, "For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said:", is about 383 pt wide in 17 pt Fraunces italic and the card's text is about 341 pt wide on an iPhone XR (from the font file's advance widths and the screenshot), so it wrapped and stranded "said:" on a line of its own, and the four lines of the poem ended where the poet's lines do and not where the card's width does, so the right edge was ragged and the breaks looked arbitrary. Nothing was wrong in the data: step 20 keeps the BSB's lines on purpose (`hydrate.ts` puts a line break wherever either neighbour is poetry).
- Decisions (the owner asked for the card as a top company would build it): (1) A verse card is a pull quote and not a Bible reader, so the card sets the verse as one flowing paragraph, the usual treatment of a verse card. Poetry layout belongs in a reader, with hanging indents; React Native's `Text` has no hanging indent, building one by measuring each rendered line would be fragile, and the Android italic-width bug in the vendor notes makes it more so. (2) `flowVerse` (`utils/format.ts`): a run of whitespace that holds a line break becomes one space, and the ends are trimmed. Not a letter or a mark changes. (3) The verse `Text` has balanced breaks: `textBreakStrategy="balanced"` on Android and `lineBreakStrategyIOS="push-out"` on iOS, which has no balanced mode but keeps a word from standing alone on the last line, as the primary button's label already does. By the font's advance widths, plain greedy wrapping would leave "willing.”" alone on its last line on a 393 pt and a 360 pt phone, and push-out and balanced are what prevent that; on the iPhone XR the text sets as four even lines. (4) The spoken label reads the flowed text too, with no line breaks. (5) The stored verse, `quoteVerse`'s rules and the share message are unchanged: the shared text keeps the Bible's lines, which read well in a message, and a check keeps it so. (6) Nothing else on the card changed: the reference, the translation pill, the type (`text-scripture`, 17/26 italic) and the colours.
- Added: `flowVerse` in `src/utils/format.ts`. Changed: `src/components/ScriptureCard.tsx` (the verse and the label take the flowed text; the verse has the two break props), `supabase/tests/profile-sync/run.cjs` (one check, 93 in all) and this file. No package, token, class name or copy change, so the stylesheet needs no rebuild.
- Measured (no phone). Red first: the new check failed on the old code (`flowVerse` missing) while the other 92 passed. After: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` exit 0; profile-sync 93. The new check proves, on the 140 strings of the seven real chapter fixtures (29 of them verses with a line break inside: Psalms 23, 46 and 127, Isaiah 41, and prose verses), that only whitespace changes, no break is left, and flowing twice changes nothing more; it also reads the card's source for the verified gate, the flowed label and the two break props, and that the share message still takes the unflowed text. A render check of the real card in a scratch harness (not in the repo) passed 9 of 9: Isaiah 30:15 renders as one paragraph with the two break props, a Psalm flows, a prose verse is only quoted, a verse that ends a speech gets only its opening mark, an unverified passage shows the note and none of its text even when the data holds some, a verified passage with no text shows the note, and the label has no line break. 13 of 13 deliberate breaks of the helper, the card and the share path were caught in scratch copies of the repo, never the repo (the card showing the Bible's raw lines; no balanced breaks on Android or on iOS; the spoken label taking the raw lines, or the text of an unverified verse; an unverified verse shown; `flowVerse` doing nothing, joining lines with no space, keeping a hanging space, squeezing every run of spaces, joining only the first break, or touching a mark; and the share message losing the Bible's lines): the suite caught all 13 and the render check 10 of them, with both passing before the breaks and after.
- Not verified: how it looks on a phone (the release build bundles its JavaScript, so it needs build 7), and how the two engines wrap the same text (Android balanced, iOS push-out).
- Known limits: a poem's line structure is not shown on the card (a reader with hanging indents would need the BSB's indentation levels, which the Free Use Bible API's simplified format does not carry); a long passage is a long paragraph.

**The app icon stays light in dark mode (2026-11-07).**

- What happened: the owner's iPhone Home Screen showed the GraceHush icon dark (a near-black plate with a muted flame), while the TestFlight email for build 7 showed the light one (a cream plate with the plum flame), and they said the light one is much more noticeable and asked for it on the phone. The phone is an iPhone XR on iOS 18.7.11 with Dark or Automatic icons (the screenshot was taken at 3:15 at night). The cause: `assets/expo.icon/icon.json` had one `fill`, so the Dark appearance of the Icon Composer document, which Xcode also renders into the fallback images that iOS 18 uses, took the system's dark background. Read from the screenshot, the flame keeps the logo colours (the plum shape and the rose centre within a few levels of the light icon, with a lighter glass rim), so only the plate was different.
- Decision (the owner asked for the light icon; the way is mine): the document's fill is now `fill-specializations` with two entries, the structure of a real Icon Composer file (one entry with no appearance key, then one with `"appearance": "dark"`, and no top-level `fill` next to it). The first entry is the old linen automatic gradient, unchanged, so the light icon does not change at all. The second is an explicit vertical linear gradient for Dark, from the same linen (`extended-srgb:0.98431,0.96863,0.94902`) to a slightly darker stop (`0.88627,0.87451,0.85098`), from 35% of the height down to the bottom. The stops were measured on the light icon of the email (flat 251,248,242 for the top third, then fading to 226,223,217 at the bottom edge). It is explicit, and not `automatic-gradient` or the keyword `automatic`, because explicit colours are used as given while `automatic` leaves the choice to the system, which is what produced the dark plate. The tinted slot is left as it was.
- Not chosen: plain images through `ios.icon` as `{ "light": …, "dark": … }` (the plugin in `@expo/prebuild-config` writes an `AppIcon.appiconset` with the dark image under the luminosity appearance). That is certain on iOS 18, but it drops the layered `.icon` and its glass look on iOS 26, so it is the fallback if Xcode ignores the dark entry (one more build). On the phone itself, Settings, Home Screen and App Library, Icon style, Light also shows every icon light, with no build.
- Source of the format: Apple publishes no schema. The structure and the key names come from a real Icon Composer file in a community repository (giginet/apple-icon-composer-skill, `fixtures/complex-icon.icon`, whose fill is an entry with no appearance and an entry with `"appearance": "dark"`) and from that repository's schema, read as data (its validator script was not run).
- Changed: `assets/expo.icon/icon.json` only. Checked by hand against that schema's rules: the base entry equals the old `fill`, the rest of the document is identical, the colours match the schema's patterns, the dark stops are light, the layer image is present. No package, native setting or code changed, and nothing was deployed.
- Build 8 (2026-11-07): built on EAS with this change (production profile, finished at 3:49 AM) after typecheck, lint, an empty release gate and every suite had passed on the same tree, and uploaded to TestFlight by the owner with an interactive `eas submit --platform ios --latest`. Run as `eas build --profile production --platform ios --auto-submit --non-interactive`, the CLI uploads the project, prints the build page and then stops with "Set ascAppId in the submit profile (eas.json) or re-run this command in interactive mode." while the build keeps running on EAS; `submit --latest --non-interactive` stops with the same line and sends nothing. So the unattended upload still needs `ascAppId` in `eas.json` (the owner's yes first, because the repository is public), and a build started that way is followed with `eas build:view <id>`, never with a second build.
- Not verified: the owner's look at the icon on the phone (not reported yet); whether Xcode honoured the dark entry (the build finished, so it did not refuse the document, but only the phone shows the Dark rendition); how that rendition looks next to the light one (the stops come from a screenshot of the light icon, not from a render); and iOS 26's Dark, Clear and Tinted looks. iOS may take a moment to redraw the Home Screen icon after the update.

**Step 36 — Grounded reflections, the incident hotfix (2026-11-07).**

- What happened: on 2026-11-07 three customers reported reflections that were generic, repetitive ("it says the same thing: it feels like you are heavy on this and that") or that had "nothing to do with what I said". The prompt (`prompts/36-grounded-reflection-hotfix.md`) traced each report to the code:
  - the five fixed Reflection headlines, chosen by the emotion;
  - a stock opening kept as a salvage;
  - a closing prayer asked for in "we";
  - an instruction that kept the person's details out of the devotional, and a tone example copied into every reflection;
  - earlier openings placed before the entry, from a person's second reflection on;
  - a transcription nobody had measured;
  - and an evaluation that could not tell a devotional written for an entry from one that only matched its topic.
- Decisions: the prompt's 18, approved with it by the owner's "Implement it", taken as also covering the migration (decision 5 asks for a yes before the migration is written: flagged). Decisions 12 and 13, the screening and writing models, are the owner's (the recommendation is below).
- Built on the server (gen-v2.3 and `screen-v2`):
  - `prompt.ts`: the sections of 1.1; no tone example; the recent block after the entry, as three lines for ten reflections; the `[unclear]` sentence.
  - `schema.ts`: `validation_line`, right after the title and required. `constants.ts`: `LIMITS.validationLine`.
  - `tone.ts`: the soft checks and their helpers, and the style measures `grounding`, `prayerVoice` and `validationWords`.
  - `output.ts`: `hardProblem`, `privacyProblem`, `personalProblems` and `readReflection`; the soft checks send one combined note and keep a salvage.
  - `contracts.ts` and `response.ts`: `Devotional.validation`. `lifecycle.ts`: `RECENT_REFLECTIONS` is 10, the line is saved, and a crisis row gets none.
  - `handler.ts` and `_shared/log.ts`: 42 fields. `export-data/archive.ts`: the line under each title in `journal.md`.
  - `_shared/safety/screenPrompt.ts` (screen-v2), with `eval/screen_prompt_v1.ts`, `transcription_scripts.json`, `wer.ts` and `run_transcription.ts`.
  - `process-entry/eval/`: `cases.json` (32 cases), `prompt_v2_2.ts`, `swap.ts` and `run_tone_eval.ts`. Also `live_check.ts`, the fakes and `fixtures/parity.json`.
  - The migration `20261107120000_validation_line.sql`, with checks 65 and 66, three PGlite variants and a 16th preflight row.
- Built in the app: `src/types/index.ts`, `src/data/columns.ts`, `src/data/mappers.ts`, `src/data/mock/entries.ts` (the anxious and weary fixtures carry a line), `src/utils/format.ts` (`firstSentence`, `getReflectionHeadline`), `src/constants/copy.ts`, `ReflectionScreen.tsx`, `processEntryCheck.ts` (the written entry's line: present, 5 to 24 words, not stock; only its length is printed), and the journal-data world and checks.
- **A deviation, to be confirmed by the download:** `src/types/supabase.ts` got the column by hand: `validation_line`, last in `journal_entries`' Row, Insert and Update, where the generator puts it. The server's contract change made the app's typecheck fail at `contractParity.ts`, as it should, and the types can only be downloaded once the owner has applied the migration. The download after the migration on the development project must change nothing in that file; any difference means the database differs from the migration, and work stops there. Until a project has the migration, the app must not run against it: its explicit column list now asks for `validation_line`, and the Journal would fail to load.
- Differences from the prompt text:
  1. The `[unclear]` sentence avoids the word "transcript", because a test keeps recording words out of the reflection's instruction.
  2. Stems: an apostrophe ends a word, so "surgery's" is "surgery" (the prompt said "surger"); -ies and -ied become -y; and -es is cut only after a sibilant.
  3. A plural pronoun in the prayer passes when the entry holds one, and a prayer with no first person at all is `none`.
  4. The swap decoys: one on the case's own topic when there is one, and one on another topic, never two on one topic.
  5. Forms of "help" and "bless" count as common words for grounding.
  6. The echo's note also says "once".
  7. A failed line is replaced by the hook, or by no line.
  8. The hook guard is unchanged, because its retry already goes to the fallback model (1.7 needed no code).
  9. The rubric's `specific_not_generic` and `affirmation_grounded` were reworded, the grader sees the first line the person saw, and regrades are keyed by the rubric's hash.
  10. After round 1 the instruction changed beyond the prompt's text in five places (round 2, below).
