**Listen in the chosen voice (2026-11-19).**

- What happened: the entry above ended with a known limit, that an answer read aloud with Listen was still the devotional's Google voice and not the voice chosen in the chat, and the owner asked for it to be fixed ("Let Fix this"). It needed a server change: `scholar-speak` read every part with Google's Text-to-Speech, and ElevenLabs' voices were only the agents of a live talk.
- Decisions (the agent's, on that request; none asked again):
  1. `scholar-speak` takes an optional `voice`, one of the eight keys of a live talk (one the server does not know is the default, as for a talk; anything but a lowercase word of at most 32 letters is `INVALID_REQUEST`), and has ElevenLabs read the part in that key's ready-made voice (`VOICE_IDS` in `_shared/voice/voices.ts`) through its text to speech, with the agents' own model and settings (`SPEECH`, moved from `agent_setup.ts` to `constants.ts`), as a WAV at 24 kHz. A reading then sounds like the same voice as in a talk and plays as Google's does. No voice id travels from the phone.
  2. A server switch, `SCHOLAR_LISTEN_VOICE_ENABLED`, read on every request and apart from the talk's `SCHOLAR_VOICE_ENABLED`, so Listen's voice can be switched on or off alone. It goes on only where the key can delete what ElevenLabs keeps (decision 4) and the Privacy Policy that says so is live. With it off, or with no voice in the request, every part is Google's, as before.
  3. The answer is always heard: a reading that fails (a malformed key, a refusal, no sound, not a WAV, or nothing within 6 seconds, `listenSpeechTiming.answerMs`) falls back to the devotional's Google voice, which still has all of its own 10 seconds (`scholarTiming.speechPart`), so a part ends by about 18 seconds, inside the app's 20. The log says which voice read it: `tts` `voice`, or `voice_fallback:<reason>`.
  4. ElevenLabs keeps every reading (its text and its sound) in the workspace's history until it is deleted, and zero retention is for Enterprise accounts. So the function deletes the item each reading names, after the response, whether or not the reading was used (`deleteSpeech`). ElevenLabs' request stays open up to 15 seconds (`capMs`), so a reading that comes late is deleted too. A deletion that fails, or a reading whose item is not known, writes a second log line under the request's id: `voice:history_missing`, `voice:history_unknown` or the deletion's own failure, such as `voice:history_http_401:missing_permissions`. Since 2026-11-21 a 404 is tried again every second for up to 15 seconds, because ElevenLabs answers 404 for an item it has not saved yet (the entry "Listen readings are deleted once ElevenLabs has saved them").
  5. The plan, the credits, the cost and the error codes are the same whichever voice reads. A heavy conversation's answer is read in the chosen voice too, as a heavy talk speaks in it.
  6. The app asks for a voice only while the account has allowed ElevenLabs. The player asks through `listenVoice()` (the chosen voice with the permission, else none), and the repository's `speak` drops a voice it is handed without the permission, whoever asks. The voice is decided once, when a listen starts, and the part fetched ahead uses it too, so one answer is never read in two chosen voices; a voice chosen while one plays is heard from the next listen. Each part is cached under its voice: `{messageId}-{voice or standard}-{part}.wav`.
  7. One permission covers both. The ElevenLabs permission's words name Listen: "ElevenLabs speaks Scholar’s answers in the voice you choose: in a live talk, where it also turns your voice into text, and when you tap Listen. Google’s AI still writes the answers, as it does when you type.", and the trust line adds "and each answer it reads aloud". The step is one component, `VoicePermissionStep`, which the Talk sheet draws and the chat's voice sheet draws first when the account has not allowed ElevenLabs. The voice sheet's line, Profile's two rows and the switch's off line say what Listen does. Like the permission's first words, these are drafts for the owner and the lawyer.
  8. Docs: the Privacy Policy (the short version, what Scholar creates, the providers' table for Google and for ElevenLabs, sensitive information, retention, and turning things off), the support page's two questions about the voice, and the legal brief. The site was rebuilt with the date November 19, 2026, and the owner uploaded it the same night (the Rollout bullet below).
  9. Nothing installed; no migration, `app.json` or native change. The app's part is JavaScript, so a reload carries it; the server's part needed a deploy of `scholar-speak` on each project (done: the Rollout bullet below).
- Changed, server: `scholar-speak/handler.ts` (the request's voice, `readInVoice`, the fallback, the deletion after the response, the second log line); `_shared/voice/elevenlabs.ts` (`speakInVoice`, `deleteSpeech`, `elevenWord`), `config.ts` (`listenVoiceEnabled`, `readElevenLabsKey`), `constants.ts` (`SPEECH`, `LISTEN_SPEECH_FORMAT`, `listenSpeechTiming`), `voices.ts` (`VOICE_IDS`) and `agent_setup.ts` (it imports `SPEECH`); `_shared/log.ts` (`voice` and `voice_fallback:<reason>` in `SpeechStatus`); `process-entry/contracts.ts` (`ScholarSpeakRequest.voice`); `process-entry/testing/fakes.ts` (ElevenLabs' text to speech and history deletion); `supabase/functions/.env.example` (the switch, and the key's two more permissions). - Decisions (the agent's, on that request; none asked again):
  1. One image under the lockup, centred, its bottom edge 36 points above the bottom of the safe area, so the logo itself ends 38 points above it, where WhatsApp's "Meta" ends on the owner's iPhone XR (measured on their screenshot). The lockup, the background, the fade and the status bar are unchanged.
  2. "from" in lowercase, DM Sans Regular 15, linen at 60% (#AFA4AB on plum-deep, 5.55:1), over the logo in linen, 18 points tall and 90.3 wide (12.53:1), 12 points apart: the word stays secondary to the logo, as WhatsApp's grey "from" is to Meta's. The canvas is 95 by 45 points with 2 points of transparent margin, rendered at 1x, 2x and 3x from the app's own DM Sans file and the owner's logo by a PIL script (`make_footer.py` in the session's scratchpad; this entry is its record).
  3. The brand only: the image says "Nouvrix", never the company's legal name, which stays in the git-ignored `docs/site/facts.json`. The source file stays untracked, like `Images/logo.png`.

A local config plugin, because expo-splash-screen draws one centred image: `plugins/withSplashFooter.js` adds the image view, its four constraints (width 95, height 45, centred on the container, and the safe area's bottom 36 points under it) and its image resource to the storyboard expo-splash-screen writes, and copies the three PNGs into the asset catalog as `SplashScreenFooter.imageset`. expo-splash-screen holds that same storyboard while the app loads, so the footer stays until the 400 ms fade into the first screen.
  5. app.json lists it first, before `expo-splash-screen`. Mods on the launch storyboard run in the reverse of the order they are added, and expo-splash-screen's own mod clears the storyboard's constraints and images before it places the lockup, so the footer must be added after that mod has run. Listed after it, the config does not load ("Cannot add mod to "ios.splashScreenStoryboard" because the provider has already been added", INVALID_MOD_ORDER), at `expo config` and at prebuild alike, so a wrong order cannot reach a build.
  6. iOS only: Android's launch screen is unchanged (no Android work before the App Store; Android 12's branding image, `windowSplashScreenBrandingImage`, is the way to add it there).
  7. No copy string (the words are in the image), and no app code, server, migration or package change.

**The Today deck of words (2026-11-20).**

- What happened: the owner sent a screenshot of the Today tab and asked for the "Your word for today" card to become a pack of cards stacked on each other: three overlapping cards in view, which a person pans and swipes to go through every reflection in the app and back, built "just as Top FAANG Company like Google, Youtube, facebook would build the UI". They asked how to see it (through Metro, in Expo Go or the development build; TestFlight needs a new build), then approved the agent's plan by pasting it back with "Go ahead with:".
- Decisions (the plan's; none struck). Screen specification 3 ("The deck of words") holds them, and Journal Data Rules the deck's reads. In short:
  1. Today's word on top, exactly as before; behind it one card for each other finished reflection, newest first.
  2. Three cards in view: the two behind at 95% and 90% of the top card's size, 7 and 14 points out (5 and 10 on a window under 360 wide), shaded at 16% and 30%. Superseded the same day: a linen wash at 30% and 55%, with a soft shadow under each card (the next entry), then 60% and 80% (the entry "The Today deck's two cards behind as plain strips").
  3. The phone's own horizontal paging scroll view, one card a swipe, not a free drag. A free drag would be the first use of `react-native-gesture-handler`, which needs approval; native paging gives the platform's own flick, spring back and rubber band, and the list keeps scrolling up and down.
  4. Every card's place, size, opacity and shade are interpolations of the scroll position on core `Animated`'s native driver, translate before scale, so no React render runs while a finger moves.
  5. Five cards mounted (one before the top card and three after it); the next page of the list asked for three cards from the end.
  6. The words kept in the phone's read cache.
  7. The heading ("Your word for today" or "From {day}") with a "Today" link back.
  8. A deck at least 300 tall; each card the next of the four player scenes.
  9. The top card's two screen-reader actions, "Next reflection" and "Previous reflection".
  10. Under Reduce Motion the cards behind do not grow or slide.
  11. No haptic, analytics event or log line; JavaScript only: no package, build, server or database change.
  - The plan's four points to confirm were built as proposed: one card per reflection (its first affirmation with a verse, else its first); a heavy moment is a card like any other, never labelled; the "Your Reflections" list stays under the deck; the feel is judged only on the iPhone.
- Differences from the plan, each with its reason:
  - The 300 floor only grows: a card with a longer verse makes the deck taller for the rest of the visit, so the screen under it never jumps while the cards turn.
  - The heading changes once a card has settled, not while it moves, so a swipe that springs back never flickers it.
  - The earlier cards' words come behind the list: the phone's own at once, the rest after one request per page. So on a new phone an earlier card appears a moment after the list.
  - The plan's "From Tuesday, Nov 12" is written as the app writes the free week's reset ("From Monday, Nov 16", `formatResetDay`).
  - Share on an earlier card draws that card's own scene. Its picture is drawn at the card's own height (at least 280), which can be about 20 points shorter than the deck draws it.
  - Android announces only the new heading (its polite live region); iOS hears the heading and the card's headline (`useAnnounce`).

- What happened: the owner tried the deck on the iPhone and said it worked and looked good, but the top card did not give the feeling that other cards lay behind it, and asked for the depth the large consumer apps give a card stack, perhaps with a shadow. - Decisions (the recommendation's; none struck):
  1. The cards behind fade toward the page, not toward the dark: a linen veil (`colors.linen`) at 0, 30%, 55% and 55% by depth (`VEILS`), in place of the plum-deep one at 0, 16%, 30% and 30%. **The Today deck shows its cards behind at once (2026-11-20).**

- What happened: the owner made a new reflection and came back to Today, and the deck showed the top card alone, as if it were the only card; only after a small pan to the left did the cards behind appear. They sent two screenshots (one card, then the deck after the pan) and asked that the deck look like the second as soon as a reflection is made, with no pan.
- Cause, read in React Native 0.88's sources (`createAnimatedPropsHook.js`, `RCTNativeAnimatedTurboModule.mm`, `RCTNativeAnimatedNodesManager.mm`): a card that is newly placed (its position changed, or it mounted) gets new native-driven animation nodes. On iOS they are tied to their view when the mount completes, but are given values only at the next `updateAnimations`, which a scroll event or a `setValue` starts, and their first frame is drawn from the JavaScript copy of the scroll position, which a native-driven `Animated.event` does not keep up to date. A made reflection changes the card set while Today is covered, so the cards behind were drawn from a stale position (off their places) until a pan sent a scroll event. A pan changes no React state, which is how the screen showed that the native side alone was stale.
- Decision (the agent's, on the owner's request; none asked again): `WordStack` sets the scroll value again whenever the cards change: an effect keyed on the cards' ids (`cardKey`), the top card, the page width, the side padding and Reduce Motion calls `scrollX.setValue(shownAt.current * pageWidth)`, which corrects the JavaScript copy and, on the native side, runs every pending connection and then `updateAnimations`, so every card is drawn where it belongs. It is declared after the effect that brings the scroll view to the top card's page, so it uses that page. While a finger or a slide moves the deck (`onScrollBeginDrag`, and an animated `goTo` to another page), the deck's own scroll events do it and the resync waits (`resyncLater`) until it stops on a page (a drag that ends on a page, or the end of a slide's momentum), so a page loaded near the end during a swipe never jolts the deck. Nothing else changed: no class name, copy, package, server or native change, so a reload of the development build carries it.
- Changed: `src/components/today/WordStack.tsx` (`moving`, `resyncLater`, `onDragStart`, `stopped`, the resync effect, `onScrollBeginDrag`), `supabase/tests/journal-data/run.cjs` (the `today:` source check reads the resync, its keys, the guard, the moves that set and end it, and its place after the scroll view's own effect), and this file (screen specification 3 and this entry).
- Measured (no phone): `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint over `src` (run directly) exit 0; journal-data 124, share-card 28 and realtime 27; the release gate prints nothing. Breakages, in a scratch copy of the repo with junctions to `node_modules` and `assets` (never the repo; the control passed first, the copy equalled the repo and was removed with the junctions first): **14 of 14 caught by a named assertion**: no resync, the resync not keyed on the cards or on the top card, a resync always to the first page, no guard while moving, a guard that never resyncs later, a drag or a slide never marked as a move, a slide to its own page marked as one, the end of a slide or of a drag on a page never ending the move, a waited resync never done, the move never cleared, and the resync placed before the scroll view is brought to its page.
- Not verified: the phone (the deck right after a reflection is made, a reflection deleted, the next page loaded near the end of a swipe), Android (its momentum end after an animated `scrollTo` was not read: a slide the deck asks for there may leave the resync waiting until the next swipe ends).
- Known limits: the first frame of a newly placed card can still be drawn from the stale position before the effect runs (the made reflection is placed while Today is covered, so it is not seen there); a resync that waits for a move is done when the deck stops on a page.
- Phone walk-through: not run yet. B0 a reload of the development build (no new file), signed in with an account that has several reflections; B1 a new reflection made from Today, then back to Today: the top card with the two cards peeking out at once, with no pan (read from the rendered tree and the deck's state, with a screenshot); B2 a reflection deleted from its screen, then back: the deck whole at once; B3 a swipe to near the end that loads the next page: no jump while it slides, and the cards behind in place when it stops.

**Gentle Piano at 100% for every new reflection (2026-11-20).**

- What happened: the owner asked that once a reflection is created, Gentle Piano be selected and playing as the reflection's background music, at 100% volume, so that a person can lower it, choose another sound or turn it off.
- Decisions (the agent's, on that request; none asked again):
  1. Every reflection this phone makes starts with Gentle Piano at 100% (`NEW_REFLECTION_AMBIENT` in `constants/audio.ts`). When the sync engine finishes a reflection (`finished`, a heavy moment included), `services/newReflectionAmbient.ts` marks it in the player store (`markNewReflection(entryId)`, the server's id). The first time that devotional is loaded, the mark is used up and the session's sound and volume become Gentle Piano at 1, whatever the session or the caller's profile had, Off included. 100% is the bed's ceiling: a gain of 0.17, about 15 dB under the voice (step 27).
  2. "Playing" is read as playing under the devotional's voice. The app never starts a devotional by itself (Audio Rules), so the piano comes in when the person plays the devotional (the mini player's play, a Journal card's pill or Today's Listen again), and it fades in and out with the voice, as every ambient sound does.
  3. After that the person's choice stands. A lower volume, another sound or Off on Now Playing takes effect at once and is saved as the default (step 27's rule). The mark is used once, so a replay of the same reflection keeps their choice.
  4. The profile's ambient default is saved as Gentle Piano at 100% when the reflection finishes (`updateProfile`: an unsent edit that the profile sync sends, like every setting). Profile's Ambient Soundscape then shows it, and the next app start begins with it. A person who had chosen Off gets the piano again at each new reflection, as the owner asked.
  5. Other devotionals keep the session's choice (step 12's rule): only the new reflection is changed, at its first load.
  6. Profile's helper under the sounds says so: "Your new reflections start with Gentle Piano at 100%. Other devotionals start with the sound you choose here." It was "This is the sound your next devotional starts with."
  7. The signed-in session starts the service after the affirmation schedule and stops it in its cleanup (the auth bridge); `stop()` (sign-out) forgets the marks.
  8. No haptic, analytics event or log line; nothing installed; no server, migration or native change. JavaScript only, so a reload carries it.

**The source step: How did you hear about GraceHush? (2026-11-20).**

- What happened: the owner asked for an onboarding screen that asks where a person heard about GraceHush, so that PostHog shows which places bring people and which of them convert, built with a modern UI and the psychology the large consumer apps use. One recommendation (the step's place, its words, the tiles, the store and the event) was approved with "Go ahead and implement it".
- Decisions (the recommendation's; none struck):
  1. The question is onboarding's second step (index 1), between the Welcome and Rhythm: after the Welcome has shown what the app gives, before anything is asked of the person, and while they still remember where they came from. Onboarding is 4 steps and Sign In the fifth ("1 OF 5" to "4 OF 5", "Step 5 of 5").
  2. One tap, never free text: a typed answer could hold a person's words, which analytics must never carry, and it cannot be charted. The eight places are shuffled once per launch at module scope, so no place gains answers by being first, and "Something else" is always last, across the width.
  3. Continue waits for a tile. Skip is always there and saves `skipped`, so a skip is counted rather than lost, and nobody is forced to answer.
  4. The reason is said, and it is true: "Your answer helps us reach more people who need a quiet place to pray."
  5. The answer stays on the device (onboarding store v5). It is sent only with consent and only once (`acquisition_source_answered { source }`), and it is registered as the super property `acquisition_source` before that event, so every later event, `purchase_completed` included, can be broken down by it.
  6. One `selection` tick for a changed answer; no haptic for Continue or Skip, no log line.
  7. Not built: the question for installs that already finished onboarding, free text, and asking again.
  8. No server, database, native or package change. One Privacy Policy sentence and one legal-brief row.
- Added: `src/screens/onboarding/SourceStep.tsx`; `assets/images/source-tiktok.svg`, `source-instagram.svg`, `source-facebook.svg`, `source-youtube.svg`, `source-google.svg`, `source-appstore.svg` (brand marks from Simple Icons, CC0) and `source-church.svg` (drawn in the Scholar icons' hand). Each file kept its line endings.
- Measured (no phone): `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint over `src` and `App.tsx` (run directly with `node`) exit 0 with `--max-warnings 0`; analytics 46 and profile-sync 96. No other suite reads the onboarding store's version or the step count.

**Twenty painted scenes, each chosen for its reflection (2026-11-20).**

- What happened: the owner asked for the reflection cards' pictures to go from four to twenty, in the same painterly style, showing people in moments a person can recognise from their own day, and pointed out that the Today word card and its shared picture use the same scenes as Now Playing, so all of them get twenty. The agent wrote sixteen image prompts in the Welcome scenes' style block (`Images/Onboarding-image/player-scene-prompts.md`, untracked); the owner generated them and asked that the scene shown for any reflection be the nearest one to what it is about.
- Decisions (the agent's, on the owner's request; none asked again):
  1. The twenty are one list, `playerScenes` and `playerSceneSquares` in file order (scene index 0 is player-scene-1), so every place that showed one of four now has twenty: the Today deck's cards and their shared picture, Now Playing's card and the lock screen.
  2. The scene is chosen on the phone, with no model and no request (`src/utils/sceneMatch.ts`, pure): words and phrases that name the situation each scene shows (strong, 3) or only lean toward it (weak, 1), read from the person's words, the title and the validation line (weighed twice) and the devotional's script and closing prayer (weighed once; a cue counts once, where it weighs most), capped at 12. A situation's scene is offered only when what the reflection says reaches one strong cue, and then gets 2 more; the seven universal scenes (a person alone in a quiet moment: 0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 19) are always offered. The hour the reflection was made leans 1.5 toward that part of the day's scenes, the feeling the model named 1.5 toward the universal scenes that carry it, and a tie is broken by a hash of the reflection's id and the scene (0.5 at most), so every phone shows the same scene for the same reflection.
  3. A picture never reopens a wound: a reflection about a death never shows the new mother, the laundry or the playground, the hospital or the man in his parked car; one about losing or longing for a child, or one the model called grieving, never shows the three child scenes.
  4. A heavy moment is shown only a universal scene, and its words are not read for the choice, so a picture never names what the person is going through.
  5. The prayer fields are never read, so a card's picture does not change when the person tracks or untracks it as a prayer; the cache key holds only what the ranking reads.
  6. The Today deck: each card shows its reflection's best scene that neither of the two cards before it shows (`deckScenes`), so neighbours in the pile never look alike, and a card whose reflection the screen does not hold shows the hour's scene; each card depends only on the cards before it, so loading older pages never changes a card already drawn.
  7. Now Playing opens on the reflection's best scene and drifts through its five best (`PLAYER_SCENES_SHOWN`), and the lock screen shows the first; the hour's scene is left for a track with none.
  8. "Husband", "wife" and travelling are weak cues: a spouse named in passing does not make a scene about them.
  9. Nothing installed; no server, migration, secret, `app.json`, copy, haptic, analytics event or log line.
- The images: the sources are 1376 by 768 (the first four's were 2752 by 1536). Each scene got a 4:3 crop the full height of the source (1024 by 768) and a square crop (768 by 768), placed by hand so the face and the hands stay inside, read off a grid drawn over each picture; then Lanczos to 1290 by 968 and 1024 by 1024, `UnsharpMask(1.0, 60, 2)`, a progressive JPEG at quality 85 with no metadata (the recipe is `make_scenes.py` in the session's scratchpad, and this entry is its record). The crops were looked at on contact sheets. Under the word card's fade the sixteen measure like the first four (`theme.ts`): the usual card at 9.7:1 or better on the brightest pixel under the headline, the verse at 8.9:1 and the reference at 8.8:1; a two-line headline over a four-line verse reaches the light part of the fade, 2.8:1 on the brightest pixel and 4.3:1 on the 95th percentile, as the first four do (2.9:1).
- Added: `src/utils/sceneMatch.ts`, `assets/images/player-scene-5.jpg` to `-20.jpg` and their `-square.jpg` crops, and `supabase/tests/scene-match/run.cjs` (14 checks). Changed: `src/constants/images.ts` (the twenty in both lists), `src/types/index.ts` (`PlaybackTrack.scenes`), `src/data/selectors.ts` (`getPlaybackTrack`'s scenes, `PLAYER_SCENES_SHOWN`), `src/store/playerStore.ts` (the track's scenes kept), `src/services/lockScreen.ts`, `src/components/today/WordStack.tsx` (`scenes` by position, and Share draws the card's own), `src/screens/journal/JournalFeedScreen.tsx` (`deckScenes`), `src/screens/journal/NowPlayingScreen.tsx` (the card's scenes, keyed), comments in `src/components/today/WordCard.tsx` and `src/constants/theme.ts`, and the checks: playback 140 (137), journal-data 124 and share-card 28 (their source checks follow the new wiring). Each file kept its line endings.
- Measured (no phone): `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint over `src` and `App.tsx` (run directly with `node`) exit 0 with `--max-warnings 0`, and the release gate prints nothing. The Node suites, every one exit 0: scene-match 14, playback 140, share-card 28, journal-data 124, ambient 68, notifications 74, offline 44 of 44, prayers 34, deletion 36, realtime 27, affirmations 13, analytics 46, ai-permission 16, billing 33, trial-reminder 48, account 23, scholar 115, profile-sync 96 and recording 68; parity 8 of 8. No Deno file changed.
- The ranking, read on the 36 made-up entries of the tone evaluation (their words only, no devotional and no feeling, at 7:00, 14:00 and 22:00): 21 led with a situation's scene at every hour (the money and work worries with the bills at the table or the desk, the test results and the caregiving with the hospital, the exam with the library, the traffic with the train, the shop owner with the bakery, the new baby with the dawn feed), the rest with a universal scene that their words or the hour chose (the loneliness and the sister who moved with the armchair, the new start with the back steps, the wedding with the park bench); the three grief entries never got a child scene, the hospital or the parked car.
- Breakages, in a scratch copy of the repo with junctions to `node_modules` and `assets` (never the repo; the controls passed first): **40 of 41 caught by a named check, one equivalent, no bad break.** They covered both heavy guards, each exclusion (a death keeping the hospital, the car or the child scenes; a lost or longed-for child, or grieving, keeping them), the prayer read, the cache key, the words' and the script's weights, a weak cue made eligible, the hour's and the feeling's leans, singular forms, apostrophes, capitals, cues matched inside words, a spouse or someone else's travel as strong, the deck remembering one card, a card with no reflection taking scene 0, the Bible scene not universal, the bakery with no cues, the content cap, the match bonus, ties not keyed by the reflection, a cue counted twice, the hours shifted, the track with no scenes or one, the lock screen on the hour, the store keeping no scenes, the deck on the hour, every card taking the first scene, Share drawing the first card's scene, Now Playing ignoring the scenes or keeping a stale stack, and either list losing a scene. The first run left four survivors, each a gap in the checks (a death keeping the child scenes, apostrophes kept, no match bonus, a cue counted in the words and again in the script); stronger checks and the file check were added, and they are caught. **Listen readings are deleted once ElevenLabs has saved them (2026-11-21).**

- What happened: the night of 2026-11-19 another session gave production a new ElevenLabs key (Text to Speech, ElevenAgents write, Voices read and History write) in the private production secrets file and set `SCHOLAR_LISTEN_VOICE_ENABLED=true` there (`secrets set`; the switch is read on every request), so Listen read in the chosen voice on TestFlight build 10. Its check of ElevenLabs' history found the readings still there. The owner approved the fix on 2026-11-21 ("Keep your recommendations").
- Cause, measured from this PC on 2026-11-21 with the production key (made-up readings of "Hi." in `warm`, each deleted afterwards; the ElevenLabs vendor note has the numbers): ElevenLabs saves a reading in its history about half a second to a second after it answers, and a DELETE before that answers 404 `invalid_parameters`. `deleteSpeech` counted a 404 as "already gone", and `scholar-speak` deletes the moment the reading answers, so every deletion "succeeded" and nothing was deleted; no second log line was written.
- Decision (the recommendation's): a 404 is an item not saved yet. `deleteSpeech` tries it again every second (`listenSpeechTiming.deleteEveryMs`) for up to 15 seconds (`deleteForMs`), each try ended by `deleteMs` (10 seconds). Any other failure (a refusal, the network, a timeout) is logged as before and not tried again. An item still not saved after the 15 seconds writes `voice:history_http_404:invalid_parameters` on the second log line, never "done". The deletion runs after the response (`EdgeRuntime.waitUntil`), so nobody waits for it. No app, migration, secret, copy or native change.
- Changed: `supabase/functions/_shared/voice/elevenlabs.ts` (`deleteOnce`, and `deleteSpeech` with its window), `_shared/voice/constants.ts` (`deleteMs`, `deleteEveryMs` and `deleteForMs` in `listenSpeechTiming`), `scholar-speak/handler.ts` (it passes the timing), `process-entry/testing/fakes.ts` (the fake history saves an item `elevenHistorySaveMs` after the reading and answers 404 until then; the world shortens the timing) and the tests `_shared/voice/elevenlabs_test.ts`, `_shared/voice/constants_test.ts` and `scholar-speak/handler_test.ts`.
- Measured (no phone): Deno fmt 230 files, lint 199, every `check` clean, the main test run 1,031 passed (1,028 before) and 0 failed.
- Breakages in a scratch copy of the functions (never the repo; a clean control of 31 tests first; the copy equalled the repo afterwards): 15 of 15 caught by a named test: a 404 counted as done; no retry; every failure tried again; a window ten times as long; no pause between tries; a try every 0 ms; no window; the handler giving no window; one retry only; time up read as done; a DELETE allowed only 1 second; a try every 5 seconds; every 4xx tried again; a network failure tried again; the handler never deleting.
- The leftovers, with the owner's yes: the two readings of the night of 2026-11-19 that production's history still held in Listen's format were deleted (DELETE 200, then GET 400 `invalid_id`), and a read-only count afterwards found no reading of 2026-11-21 left in that format. Four items of 2026-11-19 then remained, not three (01:04:11, 01:04:12, 01:04:16 and 01:09:10 UTC; character costs 8, 8, 51 and 4; three wav and one pcm, the `pcm_24000` test the vendor note records, which the first count had missed): the vendor note's measurements with the development key, made-up text in the same workspace. With the owner's yes, "four", on 2026-11-21 all four were deleted with the production key (a script checked that exactly those four matched, then DELETE 200 and a read again 400 `invalid_id` for each); the history went from 1,105 items to 1,101 and none is left from 2026-11-19. The workspace also holds the voice pack's items of 2026-11-13 and another project's items, which are never touched.
- Not verified: a reading from the phone deleted within the window (the hosted functions have only been probed signed out: the Rollout bullet below); how long ElevenLabs takes to save an item under load.
- Known limits: only a 404 is tried again, so a reading whose deletion fails for another reason (the network, a timeout, a 5xx) stays at ElevenLabs and is logged; an item ElevenLabs saves more than 15 seconds after it answers stays and is logged; the window keeps the worker busy after the response for up to about 25 seconds, inside the platform's 150.
- Hand-offs, the owner's, in this order: (1, done: the Rollout bullet below) `functions deploy scholar-speak` on the development project, then on production, each followed by the signed-out probes (401 with no token and with a made-up one, 405 for a GET, 204 for the preflight); (2) the phone check: one Listen in the chosen voice on TestFlight build 10 (the fix is server-only, so no new build), then a read-only count of the history a minute later, which must show nothing of it.

The deploy bundles the working tree, and since the 2026-11-20 rollout only this fix's three files changed under `scholar-speak`'s imports (`scholar-speak/handler.ts`, `_shared/voice/constants.ts` and `_shared/voice/elevenlabs.ts`), so nothing else of anyone's went out with it.
